name: 4NE-1

source.quote: A reservation fee secures your place in the delivery queue.

order_type.note: A refundable €100 reservation fee (credited toward the final purchase price) secures a queue position ahead of expected end-of-2026 delivery -- a preorder, not a waitlist signup with no payment and not a live cart checkout.

timeline.detail: 4NE-1 Gen 3.5 and 4NE-1 Mini unveiled at CES 2026, designed with Studio F.A. Porsche.
Reservation open for €100 (refundable) to secure a place in the delivery queue; Gen 3.5 expected end of 2026.

source.quote: secures your place in the delivery queue

promises.quote: 4NE1 Gen 3.5 is expected to be available end of 2026.

source.quote: performing a raft of mediocre or tiresome domestic chores – from doing the ironing to food prep

review.reason: The text source was reviewed, but no video segment was watched; the existing capability status and autonomy classification for the exact recorded robot variant were not fully verified.

capabilities.note: NEURA's own demo reel, alternating simulation and real-world footage. New Atlas: "It's not clear whether teleoperation was involved here, but the video does mention training the system in a simulated environment." No explicit no-teleop statement, so autonomy is recorded as unknown rather than autonomous.

notes: Degrees of freedom is reported inconsistently across secondary sources (35, 42+, 55 DoF) and could not be traced to one dated primary-source figure during this build, so the dof spec field is omitted rather than guessed.

Battery runtime is widely reported as 6-8 hours across secondary/aggregator sites, but the primary product page and reservation page fetched during this build did not state a runtime figure, so battery_runtime_min is omitted.
The manufacturer's official datasheet PDF (linked from the CES 2026 page) was not accessible as text during this build and should be added as a follow-up source for dof/battery.

locomotion left out (2026-09-21): searched the manufacturer's own product/press page and its main launch coverage (The Robot Report / IEEE Spectrum / named outlet where applicable) for a literal quote naming the propulsion ("bipedal", "legs", "walks", "wheeled base", etc.); none of the pages fetched in this pass contained a checkable sentence naming it specifically for 4NE-1 -- most pages describe height/DOF/speed without ever stating the locomotion type in words. Left out rather than inferred from photos or category. Revisit with a source that states it directly.

review.reason: Targeted searches found no confirmed model for this record; does not mean unavailable.
